sentences.text: Morphological analysis indicates this extinct bird is most similar to the modern thick-billed raven.
N. V. Zelenkov formally named and described the species in 2026 within a study titled 'A Fossil Thick-Billed Raven from the Lower Pleistocene of Crimea'.
This species represents the first record of African large-billed ravens in the region, suggesting a wider distribution for this group during the Early Pleistocene.
The fossil dates to the Pleistocene epoch, specifically living in the Early Pleistocene within the Taurida Cave deposits of the central Crimean peninsula.
